course_name_en: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering and Industrial Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the university structure and the research areas at the Faculty of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering. They gain insight into the working methods and priorities of the institutes and can relate them to the theoretical foundations developed later in their studies. In accompanying workshops, students acquire initial experience in project-oriented teamwork.
Students are able to describe the university structure.
Students are able to name the research areas at the Faculty of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering.
Students are able to explain the working methods and priorities of the institutes.
Students are able to present theoretical backgrounds in relation to practical institute examples.
Students are able to identify relevant institutes and topic areas for their further studies.
Students are able to summarize key contents of lectures on degree programs, university structure, and faculty organization.
Students are able to discuss connections between technology and society.
Students are able to correctly use technical terms and names of the institutes.
Students are able to present content on the university structure in an audience-appropriate manner.
Students are able to formulate specific questions to representatives of the institutes.
Students are able to visually and structurally illustrate connections between theory and practice.

syllabus_topics: Lectures on Mechanical Engineering and Industrial Engineering Mechanical Engineering degree programs
Lectures from the institutes of the Faculty of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering
assessment_rules: The assessment is based on active participation and mid-term tests. The specific teaching and learning methods and examination modalities will be announced in the study and teaching information system before the start of the semester.
